mechanism: A later-called higher-priority mission requests the A+B pair while both aircraft are preparing for a lower-priority mission; the paired control reverses only the two mission priorities.
hypotheses_to_test: In both variants BASIC-MISSION is called first and begins preparing a complete A+B pair at hour 7.

In late-high, SECOND-MISSION is called at hour 7.25 while BASIC-MISSION preparation is active; the later higher-priority mission takes an A+B pair containing at least one system previously assigned to BASIC-MISSION, and both mission/aircraft assignment and preparation lifecycles are observable.
In early-high, the later lower-priority mission cannot take BASIC-MISSION's required A+B pair; BASIC-MISSION launches and succeeds if no unrelated native behavior intervenes.
Each run has at most one successful mission, with cancellation and exact preparation/turnround timing determined from raw native events and reconciled to the report bins.
Source roundtrip is exact, conversion has zero errors, native reports are nonempty, stock and maintenance ledgers reconcile, and all aircraft are ready at the end.
limits: The pair is a deterministic one-unit A+A+B pool with two fixed missions and no explicit resources, failures, repair, or PM.
The expected confiscation identity and timing are hypotheses, not assumptions from the author builder.
This slice does not include predefined refuelling or payload subtasks, equal-priority ties, soon-ready maintenance, GUI-only behavior, or cross-engine parity.
